content.text:
I reviewed the whole decision pipeline and found that while the architecture was already defensive, there were **seven fail-open holes where the AI's output alone could silently drop a live encumbrance or exclude a relevant document** — the exact failure mode that produces title claims. All are now fixed, tested, and documented. Final state: **51 tests passing** (the 16 skips are pre-existing — they need sample PDFs that were intentionally removed from the repo).

## The fixes, in order of how much money each could have cost you

**1. A release could silently discharge the wrong mortgage** ([examination.py](backend/app/agents/examination.py)). Two holes here: a release matched only by *party names* (no recording reference) would confidently drop a mortgage — so one satisfaction from First Bank would clear **every** loan from First Bank. And a release whose own relevance was still uncertain (possibly about a different property) could discharge a confirmed mortgage. Now an encumbrance auto-drops **only** when the release explicitly references its instrument number or book/page *and* the release itself is confirmed relevant with complete extraction. Anything weaker becomes a provisional match routed to the examiner with the evidence spelled out.

**2. The VLM alone could exclude a document.** A confident "doesn't pertain" vision-model opinion pushed the score low enough to mark a grantor/grantee hit `not_relevant` with zero deterministic evidence ([triangulation.py](backend/app/agents/triangulation.py)). Exclusion now requires an affirmative deterministic mismatch (wrong APN or wrong legal description); the VLM can only corroborate, never decide. A missed lien is a claim — the model doesn't get that authority.

**3. Partial extractions passed as complete.** If 2 of 5 VLM batches failed, the document proceeded with whatever was extracted — a mortgage missing its legal-description page could then be mis-triangulated or mis-matched, silently. Failed batches, unrenderable pages, and page-limit truncation are now recorded as `extractionWarnings`; warned documents can't be excluded by triangulation and can't receive any confident examination role — they always route to review, with an audit event.

**4. A deed mentioning "satisfaction of…" was hijacked out of the chain.** The release-misclassification defense applied to *every* category, so a warranty deed conveying land "in satisfaction of a judgment" would be reclassified as a release and **dropped from the report entirely** — even overwriting its Schedule A role. Now only MORTGAGE/LIEN/RELEASE documents can be reinterpreted.

**5. An undated deed automatically became the Schedule A vesting deed.** Unparseable recorded dates sorted *last* chronologically, so the deed with the worst data won the most important decision in the report. Vesting now comes from the most recent *dated* conveyance; undated deeds go to review.

**6. Gateway errors parsed as empty success.** A Cloudflare 524 HTML page returned `{}` from the JSON parser, flowing downstream as a "successfully extracted" document with no data ([vlm_client.py](backend/app/services/vlm_client.py)). It now raises, which the retry/failure machinery already handles correctly.

**7. The relevance thresholds accepted any value.** A typo like `RELEVANT_THRESHOLD=0.1` would have made nearly everything auto-relevant with no escalation. Both thresholds are now clamped to sane bands and the ordering is validated ([config.py](backend/app/config.py)).

Plus two security fixes in [main.py](backend/app/main.py): the static-file path-traversal check used a bare `startswith` (which also accepts sibling directories like `static_other`), and the server now logs a loud warning at startup when `API_KEY` is unset.

Every invariant has a regression test (16 new ones), and I added a "Fail-Safe Invariants" section to [pipeline_and_triangulation.md](docs/pipeline_and_triangulation.md) so the guarantees are written down.

## Two things code can't fix — operational, for you to decide

- **`API_KEY` is empty by default and your CORS config includes a public domain** (`test.armand0e.com`). If that deployment is live without an API key, anyone can create/delete projects and read title reports. Set `API_KEY` in the production `.env` before this touches real client documents.
- **Every uploaded document is sent to a third-party VLM endpoint** (`lm.gptbox.dev`). Recorded instruments are public record so this may be acceptable, but it's a vendor-trust decision your company should make explicitly — and the report quality ceiling is that model's vision accuracy. The hardening above ensures its mistakes land in the review queue rather than in a closed file, but the review queue only works if your examiners actually clear it. The system is now fail-safe, not examiner-free — no automated title system should ever be "100% foolproof" without that human gate, and now the code enforces it.

One honest tradeoff to expect: review-queue volume will go up, because uncertain release matches and VLM-only exclusions that previously resolved silently now land in front of a human. That's the correct direction for an underwriting tool — the cost of a reviewed false alarm is minutes; the cost of a silently dropped live mortgage is a claim.

I haven't committed anything — the changes are in your working tree if you want to review the diff first.
